chunks: Ibn Abī Yaʿfūr narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:

Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “There is no spending more beloved to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, than moderate spending, and He dislikes extravagance except in hajj and ʿumrah. So may Allah have mercy on a believer who earns what is wholesome, spends with moderation, or puts forward some surplus.”

key_terms.قَصْدٍ: moderation and balanced measure in spending

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about moderation in spending and extravagance?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that Allah loves moderation in spending and dislikes extravagance, while making an exception for hajj and ʿumrah. It also praises the believer who earns lawful and wholesome wealth, spends with balance, and gives from what remains.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3621 - Ibn Abi Ya'fur narrated from Abu Abdullah (as) that he said:

"The Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) said:
'There is no spending more beloved to Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, than moderate spending. He (swt) dislikes extravagance, except in Hajj and Umrah.
May Allah (swt) have mercy on a believer who earns lawfully, spends moderately, or gives something in charity from his surplus.' "
